compliance.notes: Strongest area by a distance is the liability-benchmark work (LB-01/02/04 = 3): separate GF & HRA benchmarks built from the four balances, charted to ~2075 with a stated £10m liquidity buffer - Arlingclose-quality and a genuine sector model. Core prudential indicators, MRP policy, reporting cycle, governance and creditworthiness (INV-03 = 3, uses CDS/other data beyond ratings) are all solid, and a genuinely strategic Capital Strategy (CS-01 = 3) is in place. Weakest areas are the commercial/non-treasury and interest-rate-risk disclosures: proportionality of commercial investment (COM-03, core) is a single sentence with no quantified capacity test; there is no fixed/variable interest-rate exposure indicator (RISK-02, core); and several statutory commercial/investment disclosures are thin or missing (COM-02 paras 51-53, COM-09 investment limits, PI-08 income ratio, INV-05 specified/non-specified, BOR-03 sterling-only, RPT-05 audit-qualification flag). Context: distressed unitary under statutory intervention with Commissioners and a Capitalisation Direction; strategy is tightly focused on debt reduction and refinancing an under-borrowed (internal-borrowing ~£200m) position as legacy loans run off.

news_drafts.headline: Slough forecasts £417.4m of exceptional financial support, £336.4m of it formally agreed to 2024/25
news_drafts.lead:
Slough Council's medium term financial strategy (MTFS) forecasts exceptional financial support totalling £417.4m, according to the draft budget update report for its Cabinet meeting on 16 November. Exceptional financial support is permission from government to borrow, or sell assets, to cover day-to-day spending. The paper says: "The agreed level of EFS as forecast in the MTFS totals £417.4m".

Of that total, £336.4m was formally agreed up to 2024/25. The remainder is set out year by year in the paper's table: £15.7m for 2025/26, £42.9m for 2026/27 and an indicative £22.4m for 2027/28.

The paper says the amounts for 2025/26, 2026/27 and the indicative 2027/28 are agreed in principle or indicative. It says they will be formally agreed only once the council's accounts have been audited and signed off.

news_drafts.headline: Slough's 2025/26 overspend came in at £13.2m against a forecast £20.7m; 2026/27 budget not yet balanced
news_drafts.lead:
Slough Borough Council ended 2025/26 with an overspend of £13.2m, after applying £15.7m of exceptional financial support (EFS), permission from government to borrow or sell assets to cover day-to-day spending. The council had forecast an overspend of £20.7m. Its external auditor's interim annual audit report says the forecast overspend "was contained" to £13.2m by year end.

The auditor attributes the reduction to measures introduced during the year, including freezing non-essential recruitment and reducing agency and interim staff. The overspend was predominantly in temporary accommodation and housing benefit subsidy loss, which together came to £13.8m.

For 2026/27, the auditor reports the council "has been unable to set a balanced budget" without additional EFS, with £42.9m approved in principle. The medium-term plan anticipated a further £22.4m in 2027/28. The council's Annual Governance Statement update for the second quarter rates red its inability to produce a draft budget for November that balances within its existing EFS assumptions. A detailed report on the budget and medium-term financial strategy is due at Cabinet in November 2026. The government's commissioners at the council describe financial sustainability as their "prime concern". The council's s.151 officer, its chief finance officer, said in a report to Full Council that it is not financially sustainable without EFS.

news_drafts.headline: Slough faces material risk to reserves as services miss financial targets
news_drafts.lead: Slough's audit committee heard that the council faces a material risk of needing to draw on its reserves during the current financial year in ways it did not plan for, and that this could trigger urgent debt refinancing. The risk reflects deeper problems: housing is not meeting the financial assumptions in the medium-term financial strategy (the council's three-to-five-year spending plan), the capital programme is slipping without clear explanation, and the children's services company needs external review before further funding is committed. The auditors have also found that debtor and creditor records lack clean transaction data, making it difficult to verify year-end balances and completing a full in-year audit unlikely. The council's governance assessment rated financial management red on reserves and treasury arrangements, and amber on savings delivery and growth mitigation. Value for money findings are due in November.

findings.headline: Council Tax collected 52.53% at Q2, 0.72% behind target; Business Rates collected 52.90%, 1.57% behind target
findings.detail: The paper says the Council Tax shortfall equals £1.177m in cash terms and that the full-year target of 93.5% is expected to be achieved through additional recovery processes. It attributes the Business Rates shortfall to additional rateable value being added, which pushes the collection rate down as businesses pay by instalments. The executive summary gives the Business Rates shortfall as 1.56%, against 1.57% in the body.
findings.matters: Collection rates behind target at mid-year show the cash timing risk a finance director would track against the full-year assumption, and a lender can compare Slough's collection against the Berkshire councils the paper refers to.

findings.headline: Sundry debt balance is £10.282m, with a bad debt provision of £5.604m against £6.771m required on the paper's formula
findings.detail: The paper estimates an additional £1.167m of provision would be needed at Q2 to reach the required level. It expects the position to improve through the year due to new recovery processes. It says the Council is reviewing the formula used to calculate the provision and will update Cabinet.
findings.matters: A gap between the provision held and the formula result is a potential charge to revenue, and a change to the provision formula would affect the reported position for any council using the same method.

findings.detail: The paper lists £0.062m of HR fixed-term staffing and £2.769m for Ofsted inspection costs ring-fenced for the Families First Partnership Programme, transferred to Slough Children First. It says if no further requirement is put forward, the remaining contingency will be set against the wider overspend.
findings.matters: A contingency being forecast as fully committed to cover an overspend shows the in-year headroom is being used up.

findings.headline: General Fund reserve is forecast at £22.313m before the 2026/27 overspend, which the paper says would be drawn on if in-year mitigations fall short
findings.detail: The table shows total earmarked reserves of £39.975m after forecast transfers, including an £11m general reserve contribution that will be netted off at outturn. The paper states the Collection Fund surplus of £5.160m will rebuild a Budget Smoothing Reserve and create a new Collection Fund timing reserve of £3.344m.
findings.matters: A finance director would test the reserve position against the size of the in-year overspend, and a lender would see how far the General Fund cushion depends on delivering mitigations.

findings.headline: DfE to fund the full cost of RAAC removal at Pippins School, with £0.950m added to the 2027/28 capital programme
findings.detail: The paper states the DfE will fund the full cost, which is £0.950m above the £0.5m already in the budget. It estimates the scheme will cost £1m over the current budget, with completion projected for summer 2027 and work due to start on site in February 2027.
findings.matters: A council whose capital cost overrun is met by central government funding is in a different position from one that carries the overrun itself.
